_doc: HMTc Category 18 (Pet Supplements) compiler config for tools/standards/compile-category.mjs. Method v2.0, DOUBLE OVER-COMPLIANCE form, sitting at the intersection of two live precedents. Category 17 (Pet Foods) established that animal-feed law is a disclosed FLOOR and never the certification value, and that pet products are certified to the strictest applicable HUMAN-food maximum. Category 16 (Dietary Supplements, human) established that a supplement is certified to the strictest CHILD-protective human-food maximum regardless of the labelled consumer, because concentrated dosage forms produce high body-weight-normalised intake in a small consumer. A pet supplement is both a pet product and a supplement, so Category 18 applies both rules: every numeric cell is a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS to the strictest applicable AS-SOLD child-protective human-food sovereign maximum, and the three floors that legally govern or plausibly reach the cell — the EU complementary-feed-for-pet-animals and feed-additive limits under Directive 2002/32/EC and Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003, Japan's statutory Pet Food Safety Act maxima for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic under the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food, and the human food-supplement maximum levels of the EU, Israel, Thailand, GSO, Vietnam, ASEAN and Singapore — are named on every cell and never select a number. No cell is a `gov` cell, because no sovereign regulates a pet supplement in the as-sold human-food basis this standard is written in; the honesty of saying so is the defensibility. No cell is occurrence-derived: the hyperaccumulator and adulteration histories recorded in the scope notes inform sampling posture and never a ceiling. Basis is never conflated: the row-level basis guard admits only register rows the register itself classifies as_sold, which mechanically selects the powder limb wherever a government instrument writes its own powder/liquid split and blocks every feed-basis and reconstituted-basis row; where the binding instrument is not form-split at all, as with Israel's food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb that anchors lead, cadmium and total mercury, the guard simply confirms the row is written on the product as placed on market. Allowed provenance tags: regulatory-alignment, read-across, not-material, control, ratchet. STAFF / HMTc content, not public wiki (CLAUDE.md Part 19 firewall).

_category.name: Pet Supplements
_category.anchor: No sovereign government sets a heavy-metal maximum for a pet supplement in a human-food basis. The instruments that reach the exact cell are pet-feed and animal-feed instruments. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is the strongest of them: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food are statutory, pet-scoped and recorded on an as-sold basis, and they set lead at 3000, cadmium at 1000 and inorganic arsenic at 2000 ug/kg (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000) and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. The EU feed instruments follow (Directive 2002/32/EC complementary feed for pet animals, mineral feed and trace-element feed additives under Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003), then FDA CVM compliance policy — which is named for completeness because it is routinely cited as the US pet-food metals floor, but which the register carries no row for, so it is disclosed here as a described floor rather than a cited one and is recorded as a register gap — then China's pet-feed guidance, which is draft and gated out of the register in any event. NASC's quality guidelines are voluntary and non-binding and are not a sovereign source at all. Every one of these floors is one hundred to three hundred times looser than the corresponding value published here, and every one is named on the cell it reaches. HMTc treats the feed instruments as a disclosed floor and anchors every published cell on the strictest applicable AS-SOLD child-protective human-food sovereign maximum, following Category 17's human-grade over-compliance and Category 16's child-protective supplement rule together. Where no as-sold sovereign value exists in any jurisdiction (aluminium, total chromium, hexavalent chromium, methylmercury) the cell is a control: mandatory testing with a published method and escalation rule, and no invented ceiling.
_category.basis_family: as sold — the supplement as packaged and dosed (dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules; neat liquid for oils and drops). No reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is performed anywhere in this category.
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), pet-supplement double over-compliance form: the exact cell's only sovereign maximum is an animal-feed instrument, which is disclosed as a floor and never used; every published value is a disclosed read-across to the strictest applicable as-sold child-protective human-food sovereign maximum in the product's native as-sold basis, or a control where no as-sold sovereign value exists. Never occurrence-derived.
_category.method_note:
Why the anchor family is child-protective rather than adult-supplement. The nearest same-form sovereign analog for a pet supplement is a human food supplement, and several governments do set maxima for those. HMTc does not use them, for the same reason Category 16 does not: they are an adult-intake framework, they run one to three orders of magnitude above the child-food ceilings, and a companion animal is a small-bodied consumer receiving a concentrated dose. A four-kilogram cat given a one-gram daily supplement scoop, or a five-kilogram dog given a soft chew, sits in a body-weight-normalised intake range comparable to an infant on formula and far above a seventy-kilogram adult. That is the disclosed rationale for which analog family HMTc adopts; it is not a calculation and it does not select any number. Every number still comes from a named sovereign instrument in the register, and the instrument, the limb of the instrument, and the floors HMTc declined are all named on the cell.

Why the numbers differ from HMTc Category 16 in three cells, and why two earlier divergences are now closed. Category 16 anchors its numeric cells on the liquid or ready-to-eat limb of form-split instruments and applies those values to as-sold solid supplements. Category 18 cannot do that: the register classifies those limbs as_consumed, the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula, and Method v2.0 step 4 requires preserving the product-form split the government rule itself writes. Two of the earlier divergences are now closed, and closed by finding a stricter as-sold instrument rather than by abandoning the basis rule. Cadmium and total mercury are anchored on Israel's food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb (il_fcs2016_cd_15_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_5 at 5 ug/kg, il_fcs2016_thg_16_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_4 at 4 ug/kg), which is not form-split and which matches Category 16's published values exactly; lead was already equal at 10 ug/kg and is now anchored on the same limb (il_fcs2016_pb_16_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_10). Three divergences remain, every one of them in the lax direction, and each is named here and again on its own cell. Inorganic arsenic: Category 16 reads eu2023_ias_formula_liquid_10 across at 10 ug/kg; Category 18 takes the powder limb eu2023_ias_formula_powder_20 at 20 ug/kg. Nickel: Category 16 reads eu2024_ni_formula_liquid_100 across at 100 ug/kg; Category 18 takes eu2024_ni_formula_powder_250 at 250 ug/kg. Aluminium: Category 16 reads aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 across at 500 ug/kg, describing it there as the only government aluminium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction, while Category 18 declines that row because the register classifies it as_consumed ('portion ordinarily consumed') and no permitted conversion makes it comparable, and publishes a control with no ceiling at all — so a pet supplement certified here receives no numeric aluminium ceiling where a human supplement certified under Category 16 receives 500 ug/kg. In all three, the Category 18 basis reasoning is the more rigorous of the two and the Category 16 cell is the side performing an undisclosed as-consumed to as-sold read; the reconciliation is logged against Category 16 and is not performed from inside this config. The list is exhaustive and checkable cell by cell against the compiled records, and it names the direction of each difference rather than only its existence.

Why Israel's food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb anchors lead, cadmium and total mercury. Israel's FCS-2016 metal-contaminant table carries three limbs that could reach a purpose-formulated product: the infant and toddler formula limbs, the 'food for special dietary purpose' limb (Pb row 16 at 10, Cd row 15 at 5, tHg row 16 at 4), and a separate 'dietary supplements' limb (Pb row 17 at 3000, Cd row 16 at 1000, tHg row 15 at 100). The supplement limb is declined for the reason Category 16 declines every adult-supplement floor. That leaves the formula limbs and the special-dietary-purpose limb, both inside this category's declared analog family, and Method v2.0 step 3 then requires the strictest applicable of them, which is the special-dietary-purpose limb in all three cells. The determination is stated rather than assumed: HMTc is not applying Israel's own classification of a supplement, which would be the 3000/1000/100 limb, but Israel's strictest formulated-food ceiling, to a product Israel does not regulate at all. The full argument, with every declined limb named, sits on each of the three cells.

The two applicability filters, in order. The first is mechanical: only register rows the register itself classifies basis_class=as_sold may anchor a cell, which blocks every reconstituted and feed-basis row without any judgment being exercised. The second is declared and uniform: the anchor must come from the adopted analog family, which is finished foods intended for a small consumer. The second filter is needed because basis_class records whether a limit is written on the product as sold, not how much water the commodity contains, so a fresh-vegetable or fluid-milk ceiling can pass the mechanical filter and still be looser than it looks against an as-sold dry concentrate. The widened stricter-unselected audit scan is pointed at exactly those commodity families so that every such row surfaces in the derivation report with its disposition attached, rather than being quietly out of scope. The audit scope is now identical on all seven subcategories, so the scan is the same scan on every row and a disposition written on one row is true of that row rather than of the category in the abstract. It surfaces exactly one entry across the whole category: il_fcs2016_ias_1_milk_10, the Israeli fluid-milk inorganic-arsenic ceiling, on the inorganic-arsenic cell of all seven subcategories. It is not adopted. Every other row the earlier version of this category surfaced — hk_cap132v_thg_vegetables-other-than-edible-fungi_10, hk_cap132v_thg_milk_10, hk_cap132v_thg_secondary-milk-products_10, il_fcs2016_thg_1_milk_10 and il_fcs2016_cd_1_milk_5 — sits at or above the values now published for cadmium and total mercury and is therefore no longer stricter than any binding. A separate sweep is run outside this compiler with no scope regex, no infant exclusion and no reliance on basis_class tagging, counting a row as as-sold if its basis_class is as_sold or if its free-text basis carries the register's as-sold wording; it returns four further rows stricter than a binding in this category, and all four are packaged drinking-water ceilings: il_fcs2016_cd_17_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_3, il_fcs2016_tas_16_1_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_10, il_fcs2016_ias_16_1_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_6 and il_fcs2016_thg_17_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_1. Water is a different matrix consumed in litres per day rather than grams per dose, this category does not read a drinking-water ceiling across to a dosed concentrate, and each is named on its own cell. That is the whole set. The claim is deliberately stated in a form that can be falsified by re-running the sweep, rather than in a form that silently depends on a register tagging field being complete — the earlier version of this sentence rested on exactly that dependency and was wrong because of it.

Why all seven rows carry the same numbers. The adopted anchor family is a finished-child-food ceiling, which is defined by the consumer and the basis rather than by the ingredient, so it does not vary between a vitamin powder and a botanical blend. Category 16 publishes the same uniform shape for the same reason. The rows differ where the evidence actually differs: in the methylmercury posture (every-lot speciation where marine or freshwater material is routine, reflex speciation otherwise), in the hexavalent-chromium posture (every-lot speciation trigger where mineral, clay or geologic carriers are declared, and a lead-and-chromium co-elevation adulteration trigger on the botanical row), in the total-chromium rationale (chromium is a declared nutrient in the vitamin and mineral row and a contaminant everywhere else), and in the tin escalation rule. Occurrence history is recorded in the scope notes because it drives sampling posture; it never moves a ceiling.
_category.credible_note: The default credible-regulator set is widened by two national food-safety authorities, each because it is the only sovereign that regulates a cell the default set leaves empty, and in each case the addition makes the standard stricter rather than more convenient. India (FSSAI, Food Safety and Standards Regulations, Metal Contaminants) supplies the only as-sold child-food total-arsenic maximum and the only as-sold non-canned child-food tin maximum; no EU, UK, Codex, US, Canadian or FSANZ instrument sets either. Israel (Ministry of Health, Food Control Services, FCS-2016) supplies the only as-sold child-food total-mercury maximum in any jurisdiction — the EU, UK, Codex, US, Canadian and FSANZ child-food instruments set no mercury maximum at all — and its 'food for special dietary purpose' limb additionally supplies the strictest as-sold sovereign lead, cadmium and total-mercury ceilings on the register for a purpose-formulated finished food, which is why Israel now anchors three of this category's seven numeric cells rather than one. Each of those three adoptions moves the published value down or holds it level; none makes the standard more convenient. Both are binding national maximum levels enforced by a sovereign food authority, both are already relied on by the live HMTc human-supplement standard (Category 16), and Israel's FCS-2016 is already relied on by the live Category 25 standard. Widening the set also widens this compiler's stricter-unselected audit scan to Indian and Israeli rows, so the addition increases audit coverage as well as strictness.

pet-supplements-vitamin-mineral.name: Vitamin/mineral supplements
pet-supplements-vitamin-mineral.native_basis_label: the supplement as sold (as-packaged concentrate) — dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules, neat liquid for oils and drops; no reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is applied
pet-supplements-vitamin-mineral.scope_note: Single-nutrient and multi-nutrient vitamin and mineral supplements for companion animals, in any as-sold dosage form (powder, tablet, capsule, soft chew, paste, liquid drop). This is the row where inorganic raw materials dominate: mineral salts and carbonates, trace-mineral concentrates, marine-derived mineral sources such as calcified seaweed, and clay, zeolite or diatomaceous-earth carriers and anti-caking agents are all recognised lead, cadmium and arsenic routes, and the ceilings below are held at full strictness for that reason rather than relaxed toward occurrence. Chromium may be a declared nutrient in this row, which is why total chromium is a control and hexavalent chromium is the species that binds. Boundary rules from the HMTc taxonomy govern placement: the product must be intended for animal consumption as a supplement rather than as the sole or primary diet; anything bearing an AAFCO nutritional adequacy statement routes to Category 17 (Pet Foods); and a dental chew routes to Category 17 (pet chews), because its primary function is food or treat rather than supplementation.
pet-supplements-vitamin-mineral.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a register row the register itself classifies basis_class=as_sold. A pet supplement is dosed as sold: a scoop of powder, a chew, a capsule, a pump of neat oil. It is never reconstituted, and the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula (CLAUDE.md Part 19), so no conversion is available to make a ready-to-feed liquid maximum comparable to an as-sold concentrate. The guard therefore blocks (a) every liquid/ready-to-feed limb of a form-split infant instrument, which the register classifies as_consumed, (b) the AU-NZ Schedule 19 'portion ordinarily consumed' rows, and (c) every animal-feed instrument, whose basis is a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification. Where a government instrument writes its own powder/liquid split and that instrument supplies the binding anchor, the guard mechanically selects the powder limb, which is what Method v2.0 step 4 requires: preserve the product-form split the government rule itself writes. That is the position on inorganic arsenic (EU 2023/915) and nickel (EU 2024/1987), the two cells where a form-split instrument still binds. It is not the position on lead, cadmium and total mercury: those three are anchored on Israel's FCS-2016 food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb, which is not form-split at all, so on those cells the guard does no limb selection and only confirms the row is written on the product as placed on market. Choosing the stricter liquid limb for an as-sold concentrate would be a silent basis conversion in the strict direction, which is still a conflation, and the as-consumed limbs declined on that ground are named cell by cell.

read_across.label: Child-protective, human-grade read-across to the Israel Ministry of Health FCS-2016 lead maximum for food for special dietary purpose (row 16) — a binding sovereign maximum level written on the product as placed on market, and the strictest as-sold sovereign lead ceiling for a purpose-formulated finished food on the register. It is numerically equal to the lead action level the US FDA applies to processed food packaged for babies and young children, which is named as the co-equal confirming instrument. Adopted without any dilution or concentration allowance.
read_across.substantiation: No sovereign government sets a lead maximum for a pet supplement as such, so this cell is a disclosed read-across and not a direct maximum level. Why the Israeli 'food for special dietary purpose' limb is the adopted analog. Israel's FCS-2016 metal-contaminant table carries three limbs that could reach a purpose-formulated product: the infant and toddler formula limbs (rows 14, 14.1, 15, 15.1), the 'food for special dietary purpose' limb (Pb row 16, Cd row 15, tHg row 16), and a separate 'dietary supplements' limb (Pb row 17 at 3000, Cd row 16 at 1000, tHg row 15 at 100). HMTc declines the dietary-supplement limb for the reason Category 16 declines every adult-supplement floor: it is an adult-intake framework running one to three orders of magnitude above the child-food ceilings, and a companion animal receiving a concentrated daily dose is a small-bodied consumer. That leaves the formula limbs and the special-dietary-purpose limb, both of which sit inside this category's declared analog family — a finished, purpose-formulated food for a defined consumer, written on the product as placed on market — and Method v2.0 step 3 then requires the strictest applicable of them, which is the special-dietary-purpose limb in all three cells. The determination is stated rather than assumed: HMTc is not applying Israel's own classification of a supplement, which would be the 3000/1000/100 limb; it is applying Israel's strictest formulated-food ceiling to a product Israel does not regulate at all, and it says so. All three rows are binding national maximum levels, all three are written on the product as placed on market, and the register now classifies all three basis_class=as_sold in line with the rest of the instrument, so all three pass this row's basis guard on the same footing as the powder limbs they replace. The candidate set at the adopted value. Two instruments reach 10 ug/kg: the Israeli special-dietary-purpose row adopted here (il_fcs2016_pb_16_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_10), which is a binding national maximum level, and the US FDA final guidance action level for processed food packaged for babies and young children (fda2025_pb_baby_food_10), which is expressly nonbinding. Both are named. The Israeli row binds because a binding sovereign maximum level is the stronger instrument under Method v2.0 step 2; nothing turns on the choice numerically, because the two agree. Citation correction of record on this cell. An earlier version anchored lead on us_pb_processed-food-packaged-for-babies-and-y_10, which is a duplicate register row for the same January 2025 FDA guidance. Its status field read 'maximum level', which contradicted this cell's own prose describing the instrument as a final guidance action level, and its authority url pointed at a law-firm client alert rather than at the FDA guidance document. That row's status and url have been corrected in the register, and this cell no longer cites it. fda2025_pb_baby_food_10 is the canonical row for the 10 ug/kg limb, with fda2025_pb_root_baby_food_20 and fda2025_pb_dry_infant_cereal_20 for the two 20 ug/kg limbs. Full de-duplication of the pair, so that one register id survives per instrument limb, is a register-maintenance item recorded for the verified regulatory-fetch pathway and is not performed from inside a category config. The remaining as-sold child-food lead ceilings, all laxer and none adopted: the Israeli infant-formula powder limb (il_fcs2016_pb_15_1_infant_formula_powder_50), the EU baby-food and powdered-formula limbs (eu2023_pb_babyfood_cereal_20, eu2023_pb_formula_powder_20), the Codex cereal-based infant-food maximum (codex_pb_cereal-based-foods-for-infants-and-young_20) and the UK formula maximum (uk_pb_infant-formulae-and-follow-on-formulae-m_50). Register-tagging note, recorded because the earlier version of this cell depended on the gap. Most Israel FCS-2016 rows carried the register's canonical as-sold wording in their free-text basis field ('product as placed on market') with an empty basis_class cell, so a basis guard written against basis_class could not see them; the special-dietary-purpose rows were in that state and were therefore invisible to both the guard and this row's audit scope. That was an internal tagging gap, not a legal or basis distinction, and it has been closed: every FCS-2016 row whose basis reads 'product as placed on market' now carries basis_class=as_sold, matching the instrument's own already-tagged powder rows, and 'special dietary' has been added to every subcategory's audit_scope so the limb is scanned rather than merely named. This value is identical to the lead ceiling the live HMTc Category 16 human-supplement standard publishes, so the pet standard is not laxer than the human standard on lead. with China's draft pet-feed guidance in the same range. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is disclosed on the same footing and is the one pet-scoped floor that is neither draft nor guidance: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food set statutory maxima that the register records on an as-sold basis for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic only (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000), and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. Category 17, the live pet-foods standard this category builds on, names the same three rows, and Category 18 names them here for the same reason. They run one hundred to three hundred times above the corresponding values published in this category. They are outside this compiler's audit scan because Japan sits outside this category's credible-regulator set, not because any basis mechanism blocks them; the honest statement is that HMTc declines them as a floor, not that the machinery could not see them. The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. Of the three floors, only the EU feed rows are unreachable by construction: they carry a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification, so this row's basis guard blocks them and the audit scan drops any row whose basis names feed. The human food-supplement rows are not blocked by any mechanism at all — Israel's supplement rows are classified as-sold and match this row's audit scope — so they are declined by the declared analog-family filter alone, which is exactly why that filter is stated openly in _category.method_note instead of being left to the machinery to enforce silently.

Adopting the reconstituted FSANZ value for an as-sold powder would be a silent eight-fold basis conversion in the strict direction; adopting an additive-residue allowance as a contaminant ceiling would misdescribe the instrument. Divergence from HMTc Category 16, disclosed here because this is the one cell where Category 18 publishes no ceiling and the live human-supplement standard publishes one. Category 16 reads aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 across to as-sold solid supplements and publishes 500 ug/kg, describing it there as the only government aluminium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction. Category 18 declines the same row on basis grounds, and the consequence is stated plainly rather than left to be discovered: a pet supplement certified under Category 18 receives no numeric aluminium ceiling, only mandatory measurement and a trend control, where a human supplement certified under Category 16 receives 500 ug/kg. Category 18's basis reasoning is the more rigorous of the two, and the reconciliation belongs on the Category 16 side, which is the side performing an undisclosed as-consumed to as-sold read; it is logged for that purpose and is not resolved from inside this config.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium on every lot by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave acid digestion. Results are trended per SKU and per raw-material lot; a step change against the SKU's own established baseline, or any result attributable to a declared aluminium-bearing processing aid, anti-caking agent, colour lake or clay/zeolite carrier, triggers a formulation and raw-material investigation before release. Aluminium results are reported on the certificate rather than suppressed.

control.rationale: No government sets a total-chromium maximum for any child food or any supplement, and total chromium is in any case the wrong cell to ceiling here: trivalent chromium is a permitted and deliberately added nutrient in vitamin and mineral supplements (chromium picolinate, chromium chloride, chromium-enriched yeast), so a total-chromium ceiling would collide with a declared nutrient rather than control a contaminant. The health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, controlled separately. The complete set of as-sold total-chromium rows inside this category's credible-regulator set is: the Hong Kong Cap. 132V per-commodity rows for vegetables, pulses, cereals, meat, poultry, fish and shellfish (hk_cap132v_crtotal_vegetables-other-than-pulses_500 at 500 ug/kg and its siblings at 1000 ug/kg); the two Indian FSSAI specifications, in_fssai2015_crtotal_gelatin_10000 for gelatin at 10,000 ug/kg and in_fssai2016_crtotal_001_all_fishery_products_12000 for all fishery products at 12,000 ug/kg; and the US colour-additive purity specifications at 21 CFR 73 and 74 (us_fda_21cfr74_74_101_cr-total_50000, us_fda_21cfr74_74_203_cr-total_50000 and their siblings), which are ingredient specifications for certified colours rather than food ceilings. None is adopted. Switzerland's gelatine and collagen specifications (ch_vhk_2026_cr-total_gelatine_10000, ch_vhk_2026_cr-total_kollagen_10000) are named as an outside-the-credible-set comparator only: Switzerland is not in this category's credible-regulator set, so those rows could not anchor this cell whatever the disposition, and an earlier version of this rationale wrongly described one of them as a member of the set. The Hong Kong rows are raw whole-commodity ceilings, mostly written on wet commodities, and reading one across to a concentrated extract or dried botanical would silently change the concentration basis. The gelatin, collagen and fishery-product rows are ingredient and commodity specifications rather than finished-product contaminant ceilings — the gelatin and collagen figures reflect chrome-tanned hide processing and the fishery-product figure is a whole-commodity value — and together with the colour-additive specifications they sit so far above any plausible finished-product result that adopting one would replace a real control with a ceiling no product would ever breach. Declining them is therefore the stricter disposition, not the laxer one: what is published instead is mandatory total-chromium measurement on every lot, a reflex to hexavalent-chromium speciation, and a zero-tolerance failure rule on the species that actually carries the hazard. No number is invented; total chromium is measured on every lot and gates the hexavalent-chromium reflex.
control.reference_method: Total chromium on every lot by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave acid digestion. Any total-chromium result at or above the reflex trigger set in the category's testing schedule, and any total-chromium result that is elevated against the SKU's own baseline, requires hexavalent-chromium speciation before release.

control.rationale: No government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for any food, any supplement or any pet product. Every hexavalent-chromium row on the register is a migration limit for toys, a drinking-water maximum contaminant level, or a content limit for textiles, leather, fertiliser and electrical equipment, all of which are different matrices in different bases and none of which is a dietary ceiling. A not-material determination is deliberately not claimed: the method-artifact argument that hexavalent chromium reduces to trivalent chromium holds in an acidic reducing food matrix, but this category routinely contains dry alkaline mineral and geologic carriers (bentonite, kaolin, zeolite, diatomaceous earth, calcium and magnesium salts) in which hexavalent chromium is not reliably reduced, so the claim would not be substantiable across the row. Control is the fail-safe and is what is published: hexavalent chromium is bounded by total chromium, which is measured on every lot, and any quantifiable hexavalent chromium fails certification.
control.reference_method: Total chromium on every lot by ICP-MS. Hexavalent chromium by EPA 3060A alkaline digestion with IC-ICP-MS, EPA 6800 or EN 15192, run on any lot that trips the total-chromium reflex trigger and on any lot whose formulation declares a mineral, clay, zeolite or geologic carrier. Quantifiable hexavalent chromium at the method limit of quantification is a certification failure, not a deviation.

pet-supplements-oils.name: Oils (omega-3, fish oil, coconut oil)
pet-supplements-oils.native_basis_label: the supplement as sold (as-packaged concentrate) — dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules, neat liquid for oils and drops; no reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is applied
pet-supplements-oils.scope_note: Neat oils and oil-based dosage forms sold as supplements for companion animals: marine oils (fish, krill, cod liver, algal), plant oils (coconut, flaxseed, hemp seed, olive) and emulsions or pump-dosed liquids built on them. The product is dosed as sold, so the native basis is the neat oil, not an as-fed diluted basis. Marine-derived material makes the methylmercury pathway credible for this row, so methylmercury is measured on every lot rather than only on reflex. Refining partitions most metals into the protein and phospholipid fractions, which lowers expected occurrence, but that is an occurrence expectation and does not relax any ceiling. Boundary rules from the HMTc taxonomy govern placement: the product must be intended for animal consumption as a supplement rather than as the sole or primary diet; anything bearing an AAFCO nutritional adequacy statement routes to Category 17 (Pet Foods); and a dental chew routes to Category 17 (pet chews), because its primary function is food or treat rather than supplementation.
pet-supplements-oils.audit_scope: supplement|traditional medicine|medicated oil|nutraceutical|health food|fish oil|marine oil|krill|algal oil|\balgae|seaweed|cod liver|omega|\bcoconut|fats and oils|edible oil|vegetable oil|vegetable|\bfruit|\bfish\b|fishery|mollus|crustac|\bmilk\b|dairy|special dietary
pet-supplements-oils.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a register row the register itself classifies basis_class=as_sold. A pet supplement is dosed as sold: a scoop of powder, a chew, a capsule, a pump of neat oil. It is never reconstituted, and the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula (CLAUDE.md Part 19), so no conversion is available to make a ready-to-feed liquid maximum comparable to an as-sold concentrate. The guard therefore blocks (a) every liquid/ready-to-feed limb of a form-split infant instrument, which the register classifies as_consumed, (b) the AU-NZ Schedule 19 'portion ordinarily consumed' rows, and (c) every animal-feed instrument, whose basis is a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification. Where a government instrument writes its own powder/liquid split and that instrument supplies the binding anchor, the guard mechanically selects the powder limb, which is what Method v2.0 step 4 requires: preserve the product-form split the government rule itself writes. That is the position on inorganic arsenic (EU 2023/915) and nickel (EU 2024/1987), the two cells where a form-split instrument still binds. It is not the position on lead, cadmium and total mercury: those three are anchored on Israel's FCS-2016 food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb, which is not form-split at all, so on those cells the guard does no limb selection and only confirms the row is written on the product as placed on market. Choosing the stricter liquid limb for an as-sold concentrate would be a silent basis conversion in the strict direction, which is still a conflation, and the as-consumed limbs declined on that ground are named cell by cell.

read_across.label: Child-protective, human-grade read-across to the Israel Ministry of Health FCS-2016 lead maximum for food for special dietary purpose (row 16) — a binding sovereign maximum level written on the product as placed on market, and the strictest as-sold sovereign lead ceiling for a purpose-formulated finished food on the register. It is numerically equal to the lead action level the US FDA applies to processed food packaged for babies and young children, which is named as the co-equal confirming instrument. Adopted without any dilution or concentration allowance.
read_across.substantiation: No sovereign government sets a lead maximum for a pet supplement as such, so this cell is a disclosed read-across and not a direct maximum level. Why the Israeli 'food for special dietary purpose' limb is the adopted analog. Israel's FCS-2016 metal-contaminant table carries three limbs that could reach a purpose-formulated product: the infant and toddler formula limbs (rows 14, 14.1, 15, 15.1), the 'food for special dietary purpose' limb (Pb row 16, Cd row 15, tHg row 16), and a separate 'dietary supplements' limb (Pb row 17 at 3000, Cd row 16 at 1000, tHg row 15 at 100). HMTc declines the dietary-supplement limb for the reason Category 16 declines every adult-supplement floor: it is an adult-intake framework running one to three orders of magnitude above the child-food ceilings, and a companion animal receiving a concentrated daily dose is a small-bodied consumer. That leaves the formula limbs and the special-dietary-purpose limb, both of which sit inside this category's declared analog family — a finished, purpose-formulated food for a defined consumer, written on the product as placed on market — and Method v2.0 step 3 then requires the strictest applicable of them, which is the special-dietary-purpose limb in all three cells. The determination is stated rather than assumed: HMTc is not applying Israel's own classification of a supplement, which would be the 3000/1000/100 limb; it is applying Israel's strictest formulated-food ceiling to a product Israel does not regulate at all, and it says so. All three rows are binding national maximum levels, all three are written on the product as placed on market, and the register now classifies all three basis_class=as_sold in line with the rest of the instrument, so all three pass this row's basis guard on the same footing as the powder limbs they replace. The candidate set at the adopted value. Two instruments reach 10 ug/kg: the Israeli special-dietary-purpose row adopted here (il_fcs2016_pb_16_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_10), which is a binding national maximum level, and the US FDA final guidance action level for processed food packaged for babies and young children (fda2025_pb_baby_food_10), which is expressly nonbinding. Both are named. The Israeli row binds because a binding sovereign maximum level is the stronger instrument under Method v2.0 step 2; nothing turns on the choice numerically, because the two agree. Citation correction of record on this cell. An earlier version anchored lead on us_pb_processed-food-packaged-for-babies-and-y_10, which is a duplicate register row for the same January 2025 FDA guidance. Its status field read 'maximum level', which contradicted this cell's own prose describing the instrument as a final guidance action level, and its authority url pointed at a law-firm client alert rather than at the FDA guidance document. That row's status and url have been corrected in the register, and this cell no longer cites it. fda2025_pb_baby_food_10 is the canonical row for the 10 ug/kg limb, with fda2025_pb_root_baby_food_20 and fda2025_pb_dry_infant_cereal_20 for the two 20 ug/kg limbs. Full de-duplication of the pair, so that one register id survives per instrument limb, is a register-maintenance item recorded for the verified regulatory-fetch pathway and is not performed from inside a category config. The remaining as-sold child-food lead ceilings, all laxer and none adopted: the Israeli infant-formula powder limb (il_fcs2016_pb_15_1_infant_formula_powder_50), the EU baby-food and powdered-formula limbs (eu2023_pb_babyfood_cereal_20, eu2023_pb_formula_powder_20), the Codex cereal-based infant-food maximum (codex_pb_cereal-based-foods-for-infants-and-young_20) and the UK formula maximum (uk_pb_infant-formulae-and-follow-on-formulae-m_50). Register-tagging note, recorded because the earlier version of this cell depended on the gap. Most Israel FCS-2016 rows carried the register's canonical as-sold wording in their free-text basis field ('product as placed on market') with an empty basis_class cell, so a basis guard written against basis_class could not see them; the special-dietary-purpose rows were in that state and were therefore invisible to both the guard and this row's audit scope. That was an internal tagging gap, not a legal or basis distinction, and it has been closed: every FCS-2016 row whose basis reads 'product as placed on market' now carries basis_class=as_sold, matching the instrument's own already-tagged powder rows, and 'special dietary' has been added to every subcategory's audit_scope so the limb is scanned rather than merely named. This value is identical to the lead ceiling the live HMTc Category 16 human-supplement standard publishes, so the pet standard is not laxer than the human standard on lead. with China's draft pet-feed guidance in the same range. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is disclosed on the same footing and is the one pet-scoped floor that is neither draft nor guidance: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food set statutory maxima that the register records on an as-sold basis for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic only (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000), and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. Category 17, the live pet-foods standard this category builds on, names the same three rows, and Category 18 names them here for the same reason. They run one hundred to three hundred times above the corresponding values published in this category. They are outside this compiler's audit scan because Japan sits outside this category's credible-regulator set, not because any basis mechanism blocks them; the honest statement is that HMTc declines them as a floor, not that the machinery could not see them. The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. Of the three floors, only the EU feed rows are unreachable by construction: they carry a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification, so this row's basis guard blocks them and the audit scan drops any row whose basis names feed. The human food-supplement rows are not blocked by any mechanism at all — Israel's supplement rows are classified as-sold and match this row's audit scope — so they are declined by the declared analog-family filter alone, which is exactly why that filter is stated openly in _category.method_note instead of being left to the machinery to enforce silently.

Stricter-unselected audit disposition for this cell. The audit scan, whose scope is now identical on all seven subcategories, surfaces exactly one stricter row on every one of them: the Israeli fluid-milk inorganic-arsenic ceiling il_fcs2016_ias_1_milk_10. The general rule, stated once in _category.method_note and applied identically wherever it arises: the register's basis_class records whether a limit is written on the product as sold or as consumed, but it does not record how much water the commodity contains. control.rationale: No government anywhere sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for a food on an as-sold basis. The only sovereign food aluminium numbers on the register are the FSANZ Schedule 19 infant-formula rows — aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 at 500 ug/kg for non-soy infant, follow-on and special-medical-purpose formula, and aunz_sch19_al_formula_soy_1000 at 1000 ug/kg for soy-based formula — which are written on a 'portion ordinarily consumed' reconstituted basis the register classifies as_consumed and which no permitted conversion makes comparable to an as-sold concentrate, and the Chinese GB 2760 baked-goods and starch-noodle rows, which are permitted food-additive residue allowances for alum firming and leavening agents rather than contaminant ceilings. The remaining aluminium rows are drinking-water guideline values and a plastics food-contact specific migration limit, both different matrices in different bases. Adopting the reconstituted FSANZ value for an as-sold powder would be a silent eight-fold basis conversion in the strict direction; adopting an additive-residue allowance as a contaminant ceiling would misdescribe the instrument. Neither is supportable, so no number is invented and testing is mandatory instead. This is the same disposition HMTc Category 17 publishes for aluminium in pet foods. Divergence from HMTc Category 16, disclosed here because this is the one cell where Category 18 publishes no ceiling and the live human-supplement standard publishes one. Category 16 reads aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 across to as-sold solid supplements and publishes 500 ug/kg, describing it there as the only government aluminium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction. Category 18 declines the same row on basis grounds, and the consequence is stated plainly rather than left to be discovered: a pet supplement certified under Category 18 receives no numeric aluminium ceiling, only mandatory measurement and a trend control, where a human supplement certified under Category 16 receives 500 ug/kg. Category 18's basis reasoning is the more rigorous of the two, and the reconciliation belongs on the Category 16 side, which is the side performing an undisclosed as-consumed to as-sold read; it is logged for that purpose and is not resolved from inside this config.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium on every lot by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave acid digestion. Results are trended per SKU and per raw-material lot; a step change against the SKU's own established baseline, or any result attributable to a declared aluminium-bearing processing aid, anti-caking agent, colour lake or clay/zeolite carrier, triggers a formulation and raw-material investigation before release. Aluminium results are reported on the certificate rather than suppressed.

control.rationale: No government sets a total-chromium maximum for any child food or any supplement. The complete set of as-sold total-chromium rows inside this category's credible-regulator set is: the Hong Kong Cap. 132V per-commodity rows for vegetables, pulses, cereals, meat, poultry, fish and shellfish (hk_cap132v_crtotal_vegetables-other-than-pulses_500 at 500 ug/kg and its siblings at 1000 ug/kg); the two Indian FSSAI specifications, in_fssai2015_crtotal_gelatin_10000 for gelatin at 10,000 ug/kg and in_fssai2016_crtotal_001_all_fishery_products_12000 for all fishery products at 12,000 ug/kg; and the US colour-additive purity specifications at 21 CFR 73 and 74 (us_fda_21cfr74_74_101_cr-total_50000, us_fda_21cfr74_74_203_cr-total_50000 and their siblings), which are ingredient specifications for certified colours rather than food ceilings. None is adopted. Switzerland's gelatine and collagen specifications (ch_vhk_2026_cr-total_gelatine_10000, ch_vhk_2026_cr-total_kollagen_10000) are named as an outside-the-credible-set comparator only: Switzerland is not in this category's credible-regulator set, so those rows could not anchor this cell whatever the disposition, and an earlier version of this rationale wrongly described one of them as a member of the set. The Hong Kong rows are raw whole-commodity ceilings, mostly written on wet commodities, and reading one across to a concentrated extract or dried botanical would silently change the concentration basis. The gelatin, collagen and fishery-product rows are ingredient and commodity specifications rather than finished-product contaminant ceilings — the gelatin and collagen figures reflect chrome-tanned hide processing and the fishery-product figure is a whole-commodity value — and together with the colour-additive specifications they sit so far above any plausible finished-product result that adopting one would replace a real control with a ceiling no product would ever breach. Declining them is therefore the stricter disposition, not the laxer one: what is published instead is mandatory total-chromium measurement on every lot, a reflex to hexavalent-chromium speciation, and a zero-tolerance failure rule on the species that actually carries the hazard. Trivalent chromium is nutritionally essential and the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, controlled separately. No number is invented; total chromium is measured on every lot and gates the hexavalent-chromium reflex.
control.reference_method: Total chromium on every lot by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave acid digestion. Any total-chromium result at or above the reflex trigger set in the category's testing schedule, and any total-chromium result that is elevated against the SKU's own baseline, requires hexavalent-chromium speciation before release.

control.rationale: No government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for any food, any supplement or any pet product. Every hexavalent-chromium row on the register is a migration limit for toys, a drinking-water maximum contaminant level, or a content limit for textiles, leather, fertiliser and electrical equipment, all of which are different matrices in different bases and none of which is a dietary ceiling. A not-material determination is deliberately not claimed: the method-artifact argument that hexavalent chromium reduces to trivalent chromium holds in an acidic reducing food matrix, but this category routinely contains dry alkaline mineral and geologic carriers (bentonite, kaolin, zeolite, diatomaceous earth, calcium and magnesium salts) in which hexavalent chromium is not reliably reduced, so the claim would not be substantiable across the row. Control is the fail-safe and is what is published: hexavalent chromium is bounded by total chromium, which is measured on every lot, and any quantifiable hexavalent chromium fails certification.
control.reference_method: Total chromium on every lot by ICP-MS. pet-supplements-probiotics-digestive.name: Probiotics/digestive aids
pet-supplements-probiotics-digestive.native_basis_label: the supplement as sold (as-packaged concentrate) — dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules, neat liquid for oils and drops; no reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is applied
pet-supplements-probiotics-digestive.scope_note: Live-microbial, prebiotic and enzyme digestive supplements for companion animals in as-sold powder, capsule, chew or paste form. The metal exposure in this row travels with the carriers and excipients rather than the active: rice-derived maltodextrin and rice flour carry inorganic arsenic, dairy and yeast carriers carry cadmium, and kaolin, bentonite and montmorillonite digestive clays carry lead, arsenic and chromium. The ceilings are held on the finished dosage form as sold. Boundary rules from the HMTc taxonomy govern placement: the product must be intended for animal consumption as a supplement rather than as the sole or primary diet; anything bearing an AAFCO nutritional adequacy statement routes to Category 17 (Pet Foods); and a dental chew routes to Category 17 (pet chews), because its primary function is food or treat rather than supplementation.
pet-supplements-probiotics-digestive.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a register row the register itself classifies basis_class=as_sold. A pet supplement is dosed as sold: a scoop of powder, a chew, a capsule, a pump of neat oil. It is never reconstituted, and the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula (CLAUDE.md Part 19), so no conversion is available to make a ready-to-feed liquid maximum comparable to an as-sold concentrate. The guard therefore blocks (a) every liquid/ready-to-feed limb of a form-split infant instrument, which the register classifies as_consumed, (b) the AU-NZ Schedule 19 'portion ordinarily consumed' rows, and (c) every animal-feed instrument, whose basis is a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification. Where a government instrument writes its own powder/liquid split and that instrument supplies the binding anchor, the guard mechanically selects the powder limb, which is what Method v2.0 step 4 requires: preserve the product-form split the government rule itself writes. That is the position on inorganic arsenic (EU 2023/915) and nickel (EU 2024/1987), the two cells where a form-split instrument still binds. It is not the position on lead, cadmium and total mercury: those three are anchored on Israel's FCS-2016 food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb, which is not form-split at all, so on those cells the guard does no limb selection and only confirms the row is written on the product as placed on market. Choosing the stricter liquid limb for an as-sold concentrate would be a silent basis conversion in the strict direction, which is still a conflation, and the as-consumed limbs declined on that ground are named cell by cell.

read_across.label: Child-protective, human-grade read-across to the Israel Ministry of Health FCS-2016 lead maximum for food for special dietary purpose (row 16) — a binding sovereign maximum level written on the product as placed on market, and the strictest as-sold sovereign lead ceiling for a purpose-formulated finished food on the register. It is numerically equal to the lead action level the US FDA applies to processed food packaged for babies and young children, which is named as the co-equal confirming instrument. Why the Israeli 'food for special dietary purpose' limb is the adopted analog. Israel's FCS-2016 metal-contaminant table carries three limbs that could reach a purpose-formulated product: the infant and toddler formula limbs (rows 14, 14.1, 15, 15.1), the 'food for special dietary purpose' limb (Pb row 16, Cd row 15, tHg row 16), and a separate 'dietary supplements' limb (Pb row 17 at 3000, Cd row 16 at 1000, tHg row 15 at 100). HMTc declines the dietary-supplement limb for the reason Category 16 declines every adult-supplement floor: it is an adult-intake framework running one to three orders of magnitude above the child-food ceilings, and a companion animal receiving a concentrated daily dose is a small-bodied consumer. That leaves the formula limbs and the special-dietary-purpose limb, both of which sit inside this category's declared analog family — a finished, purpose-formulated food for a defined consumer, written on the product as placed on market — and Method v2.0 step 3 then requires the strictest applicable of them, which is the special-dietary-purpose limb in all three cells. The determination is stated rather than assumed: HMTc is not applying Israel's own classification of a supplement, which would be the 3000/1000/100 limb; it is applying Israel's strictest formulated-food ceiling to a product Israel does not regulate at all, and it says so. All three rows are binding national maximum levels, all three are written on the product as placed on market, and the register now classifies all three basis_class=as_sold in line with the rest of the instrument, so all three pass this row's basis guard on the same footing as the powder limbs they replace. The candidate set at the adopted value. Two instruments reach 10 ug/kg: the Israeli special-dietary-purpose row adopted here (il_fcs2016_pb_16_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_10), which is a binding national maximum level, and the US FDA final guidance action level for processed food packaged for babies and young children (fda2025_pb_baby_food_10), which is expressly nonbinding. Citation correction of record on this cell. An earlier version anchored lead on us_pb_processed-food-packaged-for-babies-and-y_10, which is a duplicate register row for the same January 2025 FDA guidance. Its status field read 'maximum level', which contradicted this cell's own prose describing the instrument as a final guidance action level, and its authority url pointed at a law-firm client alert rather than at the FDA guidance document. That row's status and url have been corrected in the register, and this cell no longer cites it. fda2025_pb_baby_food_10 is the canonical row for the 10 ug/kg limb, with fda2025_pb_root_baby_food_20 and fda2025_pb_dry_infant_cereal_20 for the two 20 ug/kg limbs. Sn.binding_control: Container class is a certification precondition on this cell, not a variable ceiling. The published tin value governs every lot certified under Category 18 without exception. Tin-coated or otherwise unlacquered metal-can primary packaging is out of scope for this row; no alternate canned limb is offered, and eu2023_sn_canned_infant_formula_50000 and eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000 are expressly excluded as substitute ceilings. control.rationale: No government anywhere sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for a food on an as-sold basis. The only sovereign food aluminium numbers on the register are the FSANZ Schedule 19 infant-formula rows — aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 at 500 ug/kg for non-soy infant, follow-on and special-medical-purpose formula, and aunz_sch19_al_formula_soy_1000 at 1000 ug/kg for soy-based formula — which are written on a 'portion ordinarily consumed' reconstituted basis the register classifies as_consumed and which no permitted conversion makes comparable to an as-sold concentrate, and the Chinese GB 2760 baked-goods and starch-noodle rows, which are permitted food-additive residue allowances for alum firming and leavening agents rather than contaminant ceilings. The remaining aluminium rows are drinking-water guideline values and a plastics food-contact specific migration limit, both different matrices in different bases. Adopting the reconstituted FSANZ value for an as-sold powder would be a silent eight-fold basis conversion in the strict direction; adopting an additive-residue allowance as a contaminant ceiling would misdescribe the instrument. Neither is supportable, so no number is invented and testing is mandatory instead. This is the same disposition HMTc Category 17 publishes for aluminium in pet foods. Divergence from HMTc Category 16, disclosed here because this is the one cell where Category 18 publishes no ceiling and the live human-supplement standard publishes one. Category 16 reads aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 across to as-sold solid supplements and publishes 500 ug/kg, describing it there as the only government aluminium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction. Category 18 declines the same row on basis grounds, and the consequence is stated plainly rather than left to be discovered: a pet supplement certified under Category 18 receives no numeric aluminium ceiling, only mandatory measurement and a trend control, where a human supplement certified under Category 16 receives 500 ug/kg. Category 18's basis reasoning is the more rigorous of the two, and the reconciliation belongs on the Category 16 side, which is the side performing an undisclosed as-consumed to as-sold read; it is logged for that purpose and is not resolved from inside this config.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium on every lot by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave acid digestion. Results are trended per SKU and per raw-material lot; a step change against the SKU's own established baseline, or any result attributable to a declared aluminium-bearing processing aid, anti-caking agent, colour lake or clay/zeolite carrier, triggers a formulation and raw-material investigation before release. Aluminium results are reported on the certificate rather than suppressed.

control.rationale: No government sets a total-chromium maximum for any child food or any supplement. The complete set of as-sold total-chromium rows inside this category's credible-regulator set is: the Hong Kong Cap. 132V per-commodity rows for vegetables, pulses, cereals, meat, poultry, fish and shellfish (hk_cap132v_crtotal_vegetables-other-than-pulses_500 at 500 ug/kg and its siblings at 1000 ug/kg); the two Indian FSSAI specifications, in_fssai2015_crtotal_gelatin_10000 for gelatin at 10,000 ug/kg and in_fssai2016_crtotal_001_all_fishery_products_12000 for all fishery products at 12,000 ug/kg; and the US colour-additive purity specifications at 21 CFR 73 and 74 (us_fda_21cfr74_74_101_cr-total_50000, us_fda_21cfr74_74_203_cr-total_50000 and their siblings), which are ingredient specifications for certified colours rather than food ceilings. None is adopted. Switzerland's gelatine and collagen specifications (ch_vhk_2026_cr-total_gelatine_10000, ch_vhk_2026_cr-total_kollagen_10000) are named as an outside-the-credible-set comparator only: Switzerland is not in this category's credible-regulator set, so those rows could not anchor this cell whatever the disposition, and an earlier version of this rationale wrongly described one of them as a member of the set. The Hong Kong rows are raw whole-commodity ceilings, mostly written on wet commodities, and reading one across to a concentrated extract or dried botanical would silently change the concentration basis. The gelatin, collagen and fishery-product rows are ingredient and commodity specifications rather than finished-product contaminant ceilings — the gelatin and collagen figures reflect chrome-tanned hide processing and the fishery-product figure is a whole-commodity value — and together with the colour-additive specifications they sit so far above any plausible finished-product result that adopting one would replace a real control with a ceiling no product would ever breach. Declining them is therefore the stricter disposition, not the laxer one: what is published instead is mandatory total-chromium measurement on every lot, a reflex to hexavalent-chromium speciation, and a zero-tolerance failure rule on the species that actually carries the hazard. Trivalent chromium is nutritionally essential and the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, controlled separately. No number is invented; total chromium is measured on every lot and gates the hexavalent-chromium reflex.
control.reference_method: Total chromium on every lot by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave acid digestion. Any total-chromium result at or above the reflex trigger set in the category's testing schedule, and any total-chromium result that is elevated against the SKU's own baseline, requires hexavalent-chromium speciation before release.

control.rationale: No government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for any food, any supplement or any pet product. Every hexavalent-chromium row on the register is a migration limit for toys, a drinking-water maximum contaminant level, or a content limit for textiles, leather, fertiliser and electrical equipment, all of which are different matrices in different bases and none of which is a dietary ceiling. A not-material determination is deliberately not claimed: the method-artifact argument that hexavalent chromium reduces to trivalent chromium holds in an acidic reducing food matrix, but this category routinely contains dry alkaline mineral and geologic carriers (bentonite, kaolin, zeolite, diatomaceous earth, calcium and magnesium salts) in which hexavalent chromium is not reliably reduced, so the claim would not be substantiable across the row. Control is the fail-safe and is what is published: hexavalent chromium is bounded by total chromium, which is measured on every lot, and any quantifiable hexavalent chromium fails certification.
control.reference_method: Total chromium on every lot by ICP-MS. Hexavalent chromium by EPA 3060A alkaline digestion with IC-ICP-MS, EPA 6800 or EN 15192, run on any lot that trips the total-chromium reflex trigger and on any lot whose formulation declares a mineral, clay, zeolite or geologic carrier. Quantifiable hexavalent chromium at the method limit of quantification is a certification failure, not a deviation.

pet-supplements-botanical-herbal.name: Botanical/herbal blends
pet-supplements-botanical-herbal.native_basis_label: the supplement as sold (as-packaged concentrate) — dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules, neat liquid for oils and drops; no reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is applied
pet-supplements-botanical-herbal.scope_note: Botanical and herbal supplements and blends for companion animals: dried whole herb, powdered rhizome and root, standardised extracts, tinctures and glycerites, in as-sold form. This row carries two independent metal routes. The first is soil uptake, which is why leaf, root and rhizome material hyperaccumulates lead, cadmium and arsenic and why concentrating an extract concentrates the metal with it. The second is deliberate adulteration: lead chromate has a documented history as a colourant in dried rhizome and root spice material, which introduces lead and hexavalent chromium together and is the reason this row's chromium controls run at their strictest posture. Neither route relaxes a ceiling. Boundary rules from the HMTc taxonomy govern placement: the product must be intended for animal consumption as a supplement rather than as the sole or primary diet; anything bearing an AAFCO nutritional adequacy statement routes to Category 17 (Pet Foods); and a dental chew routes to Category 17 (pet chews), because its primary function is food or treat rather than supplementation.
pet-supplements-botanical-herbal.audit_scope: supplement|traditional medicine|medicated oil|nutraceutical|health food|botanical|herbal|\bherbs?\b|\bspice|turmeric|curcum|ginger|\btea\b|\bteas\b|root and rhizome|rhizome|dried plant|plant extract|milk thistle|ashwagandha|vegetable|edible fungi|\bfungi|\bfruit|leafy|\broots?\b|\bcereal|\bmilk\b|dairy|special dietary
pet-supplements-botanical-herbal.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a register row the register itself classifies basis_class=as_sold. A pet supplement is dosed as sold: a scoop of powder, a chew, a capsule, a pump of neat oil. It is never reconstituted, and the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula (CLAUDE.md Part 19), so no conversion is available to make a ready-to-feed liquid maximum comparable to an as-sold concentrate. The guard therefore blocks (a) every liquid/ready-to-feed limb of a form-split infant instrument, which the register classifies as_consumed, (b) the AU-NZ Schedule 19 'portion ordinarily consumed' rows, and (c) every animal-feed instrument, whose basis is a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification. Where a government instrument writes its own powder/liquid split and that instrument supplies the binding anchor, the guard mechanically selects the powder limb, which is what Method v2.0 step 4 requires: preserve the product-form split the government rule itself writes. That is the position on inorganic arsenic (EU 2023/915) and nickel (EU 2024/1987), the two cells where a form-split instrument still binds. It is not the position on lead, cadmium and total mercury: those three are anchored on Israel's FCS-2016 food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb, which is not form-split at all, so on those cells the guard does no limb selection and only confirms the row is written on the product as placed on market. Choosing the stricter liquid limb for an as-sold concentrate would be a silent basis conversion in the strict direction, which is still a conflation, and the as-consumed limbs declined on that ground are named cell by cell.

read_across.label: Child-protective, human-grade read-across to the Israel Ministry of Health FCS-2016 lead maximum for food for special dietary purpose (row 16) — a binding sovereign maximum level written on the product as placed on market, and the strictest as-sold sovereign lead ceiling for a purpose-formulated finished food on the register. It is numerically equal to the lead action level the US FDA applies to processed food packaged for babies and young children, which is named as the co-equal confirming instrument. Adopted without any dilution or concentration allowance.
read_across.substantiation: No sovereign government sets a lead maximum for a pet supplement as such, so this cell is a disclosed read-across and not a direct maximum level. Why the Israeli 'food for special dietary purpose' limb is the adopted analog. Israel's FCS-2016 metal-contaminant table carries three limbs that could reach a purpose-formulated product: the infant and toddler formula limbs (rows 14, 14.1, 15, 15.1), the 'food for special dietary purpose' limb (Pb row 16, Cd row 15, tHg row 16), and a separate 'dietary supplements' limb (Pb row 17 at 3000, Cd row 16 at 1000, tHg row 15 at 100). HMTc declines the dietary-supplement limb for the reason Category 16 declines every adult-supplement floor: it is an adult-intake framework running one to three orders of magnitude above the child-food ceilings, and a companion animal receiving a concentrated daily dose is a small-bodied consumer. That leaves the formula limbs and the special-dietary-purpose limb, both of which sit inside this category's declared analog family — a finished, purpose-formulated food for a defined consumer, written on the product as placed on market — and Method v2.0 step 3 then requires the strictest applicable of them, which is the special-dietary-purpose limb in all three cells. The determination is stated rather than assumed: HMTc is not applying Israel's own classification of a supplement, which would be the 3000/1000/100 limb; it is applying Israel's strictest formulated-food ceiling to a product Israel does not regulate at all, and it says so. All three rows are binding national maximum levels, all three are written on the product as placed on market, and the register now classifies all three basis_class=as_sold in line with the rest of the instrument, so all three pass this row's basis guard on the same footing as the powder limbs they replace. The candidate set at the adopted value. Two instruments reach 10 ug/kg: the Israeli special-dietary-purpose row adopted here (il_fcs2016_pb_16_food_for_special_dietary_purpose_10), which is a binding national maximum level, and the US FDA final guidance action level for processed food packaged for babies and young children (fda2025_pb_baby_food_10), which is expressly nonbinding. Both are named. The Israeli row binds because a binding sovereign maximum level is the stronger instrument under Method v2.0 step 2; nothing turns on the choice numerically, because the two agree. Citation correction of record on this cell. An earlier version anchored lead on us_pb_processed-food-packaged-for-babies-and-y_10, which is a duplicate register row for the same January 2025 FDA guidance. Its status field read 'maximum level', which contradicted this cell's own prose describing the instrument as a final guidance action level, and its authority url pointed at a law-firm client alert rather than at the FDA guidance document. That row's status and url have been corrected in the register, and this cell no longer cites it. fda2025_pb_baby_food_10 is the canonical row for the 10 ug/kg limb, with fda2025_pb_root_baby_food_20 and fda2025_pb_dry_infant_cereal_20 for the two 20 ug/kg limbs. Full de-duplication of the pair, so that one register id survives per instrument limb, is a register-maintenance item recorded for the verified regulatory-fetch pathway and is not performed from inside a category config. The remaining as-sold child-food lead ceilings, all laxer and none adopted: the Israeli infant-formula powder limb (il_fcs2016_pb_15_1_infant_formula_powder_50), the EU baby-food and powdered-formula limbs (eu2023_pb_babyfood_cereal_20, eu2023_pb_formula_powder_20), the Codex cereal-based infant-food maximum (codex_pb_cereal-based-foods-for-infants-and-young_20) and the UK formula maximum (uk_pb_infant-formulae-and-follow-on-formulae-m_50).
